newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arabs, Jews accuse Israel of torture.
newsitem.headline: Arabs, Jews accuse Israel of torture.

text.p: Arabs and Jews have accused Israeli secret police interrogators of using torture to extract confessions from suspects.

Israel's High Court on Friday issued an interim order preventing Shin Bet secret police from using "physical force" against a Palestinian student arrested two weeks ago, court spokesman Moshe Gorali said.

In a separate case, an Israeli lawyer on Friday charged interrogators had used "coercion and violence" to extract confessions from ultranationalist Jewish youths imprisoned for killing an Arab in a 1992 grenade attack.

Palestinian Mustafa Hassan Mohammed Abu Nasr charged Israeli police had tortured him since his arrest in the West Bank two weeks ago and issued an emergency appeal on Thursday to Israel's High Court to stop it.

"The court issued an interim order preventing the use of physical force against the petitioner," Gorali told Reuters. He said the interim order would remain in force until a general hearing, which had not yet been scheduled.

In his petition Abu Nasr, from Jabalya refugee camp in Gaza, said he was made to sit on a low stool with a sack over his head, his legs shackled and arms stretched behind his back and also hung for hours from his cell door, Israel Radio said.
Deputy state prosecutor Shai Nitzan told the court Abu Nasr was being held because police suspected he had information which could help prevent guerrilla attacks, Israel's army radio said.

A 1987 Israeli commission ruled the Shin Bet could use "moderate physical pressure" in interrogations and "increased physical pressure" when an attack was imminent. Human rights groups have said the commission's report sanctioned torture.

Israeli lawyer Avraham Sion told Reuters on Friday he had appealed to the High Court to overturn convictions of four Jews who confessed under force to killing a Palestinian and wounding seven in a grenade attack in Jerusalem's Old City in 1992.
"The confessions were taken under pressure and are therefore inadmissible under Israeli law," Sion said.

Sion said he had acquired audio tapes of Shin Bet interrogations of the four, who belonged to the now outlawed anti-Arab Kach movement, from prosecutors. He said his clients had been deprived of sleep in rancid cells, beaten, and burned with hot coffee.

Israel's Army radio broadcast some of the tapes on Friday. At one point, loud noises are heard followed by sobs and gasps. The tapes broadcast also contained one youth's unrepentant confession. The four, minors aged 15 to 16 at the time of the attack, were sentenced to between five and 15 years in jail.

Israel's Maariv daily published excerpts of a new book by a reserve army colonel who alleges Israel tortures its own navy commandos during exercises to prepare them in case of capture by enemy forces.

"They told me that from now on my name is 'whore number 25'. It was like that with all of us," the newspaper quoted one officer as saying in the book, referring to Shin Bet secret police officials who conducted the exercise.

"We had to run in place. Whoever didn't run was beaten. When we had to urinate, they told us to do it on our friends or be beaten. In another instance to lick our own urine. We spent four days with sacks on our head," he was quoted as saying.
The Israeli army refused to comment.
